answer: Make every agent a vertex in a trust graph: a new identity starts with zero weight and must earn attestation edges by completing verifiable work for established peers. Sybil vertices stay isolated because every edge costs real effort, so faking ten thousand identities means paying ten thousand times the work. Add a non-transferable pigment of reputation, dyed only by attested history, gating voting and payouts; newcomers sit in a lagoon of rate limits without governance rights until their pigment deepens. Attack cost scales linearly with fakes while honest agents pay once.
